newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans two more sugar plants in Uzbekistan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans two more sugar plants in Uzbekistan.

text.p: Turkey's state-run sugar refineries, Turkseker, are in talks with the Uzbek government to establish two more refineries in the ex-Soviet republic, Turkseker officials said on Friday.
"There is already one being built. We have also exchanged intents for two more plants in Uzbekistan," said a senior Turkseker official.
"One of them will be near Samarkand and the other one will be near Namangan," he told Reuters.
He said the plants would have daily beet processing capacities of 3,000 tonnes and 6,000 tonnes. He said talks were continuing but other details were not clear yet.
Turkseker and the local contractor Yuksel Insaat have been building a sugar plant in Druzhba in a joint venture with Uzbekistan's state company Pishcheprom for about $100 million.
"There is no obstacle preventing the factory becoming operational from 1998," the official said.
All machinery and other equipment will be transferred from Turkey for the plant, which will have a daily beet processing capacity of 3,000 tonnes, he said.
The plant will be owned by Uzbekistan, which will pay back Turkey's contribution of about $83 million in terms of sugar.
Pishcheprom officials have said there are plans to raise the plant's capacity to 150,000 tonnes per year based on imports of raw sugar from the Caribbean, mainly Cuba.
